Isaac Bashevis Singer, a 1978 winner of the Nobel Prize for 
literature and a leading ﬁ gure in Yiddish literature, was a 
resident of the Town in the 1980s. Now the Surfside street 
named in his honor has new, more prominent signage. A 
brief ceremony attended by residents and Town oﬃ  cials 
marked the unveiling of the signs on 95th Street. In ad-
dition to the Nobel prize, Singer also won two National 
Book Awards for his novels and short story collections. He 
died on July 24, 1991.
(L-R) Special Projects Director 
Randy Stokes, Commissioner 
Marta Olchyk and Town Man-
ager Mike Crotty join residents 
at the unveiling.
On  July 17th  a public meeting was held 
to discuss the possibility of creating a Business 
Improvement District (BID) for Downtown Surfside.
Redevelopment Management Associates (RMA) 
presented information on how BIDs work and 
described possible BID programs for Downtown 
Surfside. Similar to a Homeowners Association, but 
for commercial properties, a BID formalizes a process 
for property and business owners to work together to 
improve a commercial district.     
Property and business owners will ﬁ nalize plans 
for a BID and bring the project for approval by the 
Town Commission.  For more information, contact 
Duncan Tavares - Tourism, Economic Development & 
Community Services Director - at 305-864-0722.
Joining the list of popular culinary establishments 
in the downtown district is Ike’s Diner, located at 9476 
Harding Avenue. The Diner was created by a partnership 
between long-time restaurateur Samir Elnomany  and 
Kosher Chef Yossi Horowitz. The diner serves breakfast all 
day, pastas, salads, pizzas, ﬁ sh, sandwiches, ice cream by 
the scoop and delicious iced coﬀ ees. Ike’s Diner is serving 
from 7:30 a.m. – 11 p.m. every day except Saturday. Home 
deliveries are available.  For more information, call (305) 
397-8559.

Streetscape Improvement Takes Next Step
The plans for the Harding Avenue Streetscape are 
now being reviewed by the  Florida Department of 
Transportation, since Harding Avenue is a state-owned 
street.  The Town is planning to start the project as soon 
as it is approved by the Florida DOT. 
Designed by the ﬁ rms of Stantac and Rosenberg 
Gradner, the Harding Avenue Streetscape plan will 
transform the downtown area with Medjool palms, 
colorful tropical shrubs and pocket parks with benches, 
pavers and street crossings. 
The Town Commission has approved renovations 
and new landscaping for two major parking lots in 
the downtown Surfside district. The ﬁ rst is the Abbott 
lot between 95th and 96th Streets (west of Harding 
Avenue behind the CVS and Flanigan’s). The other is 
the 94th Street lot (on the southeast corner of 94th and 
Harding Avenue).   Contractors Lynx Construction and 
Luke’s Landscaping will be working with Public Works 
to complete the renovation. The project is scheduled to 
begin before the end of August.
